video_title: Charles Barkley on "Inside the NBA" on ESPN, Draymond Diss, & More

quotes.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Barkley on the Knicks-Cavaliers series and the positive impact of a Knicks Finals appearance
quotes.excerpt: Worst case scenario, I'm not going to lie, I don't think it'd be the worst thing in the world for the Knicks to get to the Finals.
quotes.quote: I'm excited. Looking forward, we got obviously Game 1, Knicks, Cavs. Should be an interesting series. You know, I picked Cleveland coming in. They make me nervous, man, because they, you talk about Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde, they are the ultimate Jekyll and Hyde team. But you know what? Worst case scenario, I'm not going to lie, I don't think it'd be the worst thing in the world for the Knicks to get to the Finals. I think it'd be great for the NBA.

quotes.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Barkley praises New York fans and the Madison Square Garden atmosphere
quotes.excerpt: Being back in New York, I have forgot how amazing the Garden is when the Knicks are doing good.

text_blocks.speaker: JIMMY TRAINA
text_blocks.text: Being back in New York.

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: Being back in New York, I have forgot how amazing the Garden is when the Knicks are doing good. It was incredible. It was incredible.

text_blocks.speaker: JIMMY TRAINA
text_blocks.text: Yeah, the fans have been out of control. I mean, those those videos you see outside of Madison Square Garden.

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: Let me tell you something. I'm going to tell you how crazy New York fans are. So we're in Atlanta and so after they lose Game 3, people are walking around around the hotel, 'I can't believe we got rid of Thibs, we got to fire Mike Brown, we got to find a way to get Giannis.' This was after Game 3 when they were down 2-1. They win the next game, then obviously they close it. 'We're going to the championship.' I said, 'Well, you've got another series in between.' But New York, man, you're right, they're different.

quotes.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Barkley on Knicks fans' high expectations and the Cavaliers series being a tougher test
quotes.excerpt: I don't think the Knicks fan understands how good Oklahoma City and San Antonio... that's another level than they've seen here with the Hawks, the Sixers and the Cavaliers.

text_blocks.speaker: JIMMY TRAINA
text_blocks.text: I don't think the Knicks fan understands, I mean, maybe after last night they do, how good Oklahoma City and San Antonio, like that's another level than they've seen here with the Hawks, the Sixers and the Cavaliers in my opinion. I don't know what you think, but don't, you know, sometimes the Knicks fan likes to act like a championship has been won. Be careful.

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: Yeah, actually, I 100% agree with you. Actually, I think the Cavaliers series for the Knicks is going to be a step up because, you know, Atlanta's got a bright future, but they're not ready yet. The Knicks, then obviously the Sixers, Joel's not healthy and that's a tough, but the Cavs are going to be a tough test. But man, let me tell you something. I was so excited to watch that game last night.

quotes.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Barkley dismisses the "rest vs. rust" debate, stating rest is always physically beneficial
quotes.excerpt: I don't believe in rust rest thing. I've been BSing for a long time.
quotes.quote: I don't believe in rust rest thing because I, you know, I've been I've been BSing for a long time when going back in my 40 years. If the team wins the first game, they say the rest did them good. If they lose, they say they were rusty. So I don't believe in the BS that goes with that. The only thing you lose is a little bit of competitive edge. The rest is always going to do you good from a physical standpoint. But you do lose a little competitive edge, but I think, you know, you're in the conference finals, you should be ready to go, period.

quotes.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Barkley praises Victor Wembanyama's historic double-overtime performance in the Conference Finals
quotes.excerpt: I was talking to Mike Tirico the other day and I said, 'Yo, man, I'm so that's this a big boy heavyweight slugfest.'

text_blocks.speaker: JIMMY TRAINA
text_blocks.text: Funny thing is, you ended up becoming a little bit part of a little part of the story because Wemby with the 41, 24 points, first guy to do 35-20 in a Conference Final game since 1993, and the gentleman who did it was Charles Barkley.

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: Yeah, that was a, when I saw that, that was a very nice thing, bring back some great memories, great, great memories. Hey, you know, I was talking to Mike Tirico the other day and I said, 'Yo, man, I'm so that's this a big boy heavyweight slugfest.' And I think after watching that game last night, double overtime and Wemby do what he did, I could go for seven more of those. I could, I could go for seven more of those. We knew it was going to be a heavyweight slugfest, and it was a heavyweight slugfest right out of the shoot. So I can't wait. But like I say, but I'm not going to sleep because every series is different. Like people assume that is for the championship. I said, 'Yo, man, you can't sleep on the Knicks or the Cavs.' Because every series is different. I mean, you you assume like, 'Yeah,' I heard some people saying, 'That's for the championship.' I said, 'You know, hey, don't sleep on that, man, because anything can happen.' But man, I was excited to watch that game last night. I'm excited for our game tonight because the Conference Finals are special because you're what, it's kind of like the Final Four in college basketball, you put all that time and effort into it, and you're this close to the Finals. And for one of these, for two of these teams, it's going to be heartbreaking. Oh, it was definitely historic. Number one, his first like, and and you you you factor in because I was part, I wasn't part of it, but I remember the night that David Robinson got MVP and Hakeem went crazy because he thought he should have won MVP. It was kind of like that last night with Victor and Shai. I mean, you couldn't have scripted it any better. I mean, you think about that. It was the exact same situation with David and Hakeem, and Shai and Victor. You're like, 'Oh,' and I remember Hakeem Hakeem had said, he says, 'They're giving that man my trophy.' And hey, which is one of the great lines of all time. He says, 'I can't believe they're giving that man my trophy.' And Victor, and the thing I love about Victor, number one, he's humble, but he speaks the truth. When the reporter asked him last night, you know, when Shai was getting the MVP, were you thinking that should have been my trophy? He says, he just says, 'Yes.' I love that too. But man, listen, I was surprised how big a margin Shai won the MVP by. Because I thought there was four guys should have gotten votes. The obviously Victor and Wemby and Nikola Jokic and Jaylen Brown. I thought those four guys, if you voted for one of those four guys, you would have had a compelling argument. But I was really surprised Shai won it as easily as he did. And Victor came in third, he didn't come in second.

quotes.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Barkley criticizes the NBA's disjointed schedule across multiple platforms, calling it unfair to fans
quotes.excerpt: I think that Adam Silver's got to get a hold of this thing. I think the games are too disjointed right now.

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: I think that Adam Silver's got to get a hold of this thing. I think the games are too disjointed right now. Like NBC, Peacock, Amazon, we've got, I think we we have disrespected the fans. They don't know when the games are on. I just think that's really unfair to the fans. And I understand, Adam, I love Adam. Adam's a great guy. But he he took the most money, but man, it it's hard for, like, for me. Like, when we weren't having games, I had to go, I had to go to my app and see where the game was at.

text_blocks.speaker: JIMMY TRAINA
text_blocks.text: Is it on NBC? Is it on Peacock? Is it on Amazon? The nights we haven't been working. So it's been frustrating for me. I can't imagine how frustrating it is for the regular fan. And I think we I'm not sure what the solution is because we they've taken all the money now, but they've got to do something because I think we've done a disservice to the fans. Yeah, early in the playoffs, it's a mess. I mean, now we're in a good spot because you guys, ESPN/ABC has the East. We know NBC has the West, so you don't have to think about it.

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: Now, so let me ask you a question. So I don't even know this. I'm just asking. Do do NBC have exclusive or they have to share with Amazon?

text_blocks.speaker: JIMMY TRAINA
text_blocks.text: They they are, if I'm not mistaken, they they will be rotating every next year, Prime Video will have a Conference Final, NBC will not.

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: Okay, okay. See, it's hard to keep up with it, man. I didn't even know that. I asked that question. At least that's a little bit better. Now, are they going to show all the games on NBC?

text_blocks.speaker: JIMMY TRAINA
text_blocks.text: I believe, yeah, they they won't do a Peacock exclusive for the Western Conference Final.

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: And they should not. It should be on NBC.

quotes.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Barkley defends "Inside the NBA" content, emphasizing entertainment over constant X's and O's
quotes.excerpt: We're trying to entertain people. Do people really want to see us four dummies sit there from 7:00 to 2:00 in the morning and talk about picks and roll, blitzes, over under, elbow wings and things like that?

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: I don't know about that. I mean, I I think when you don't see us enough, it's hard to get assume what's happening is happening, to be honest with you. I don't think we changed anything. You know, it's interesting, for what it's worth, I've had a great time with ESPN. I think all the guys have. You know, they come and watch the show. I asked them, 'Hey, y'all happy with everything?' Because we're in a relationship, I want it to work for everybody. You know, I've called Burke, you know, I've called Tim Corrigan. I said, 'Hey, is there anything y'all unhappy with or want us to change?' And as long as they're happy, listen, we ain't going to, I don't think we've changed anything. But listen, man, the most the most the number one thing is always be the game. Our job, number one, we want people to have fun. You know, we're trying to entertain people. I think the people don't understand, we're on television from 7:00 to 2:00 in the damn morning. What how much basketball, first of all, how many people actually know a damn thing enough about basketball for us to X and O them from 7:00 to 2:00 in the morning? So we try to split it up, and number one, we hope we have a great game. But we have an obligation to entertain people too. I mean, do do people really want to see us four dummies sit there from 7:00 to 2:00 in the morning and talk about picks and roll, blitzes, over under, elbow wings and things like that? So so so listen, man, I I I want people to have fun watching basketball, period.

text_blocks.speaker: JIMMY TRAINA
text_blocks.text: It's different strokes for different folks. I mean, I much prefer the entertainment. I listen, anytime you call Shaq a fool, I laugh. So I'll take that over a pick and roll. The word fool is not used enough as an insult. And it is a great insult. You know, it's not too nasty.

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: No, it's not.

text_blocks.speaker: JIMMY TRAINA
text_blocks.text: But it's a perfect shot to get at someone.

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: Yeah. And I love getting the shot, and I love calling Kenny that too. But like I say, Jimmy, you just hit the nail on the head. Man, we're trying to entertain people. We I listen, because there's two different audience. I've always said this, there's two different audience in my opinion. There's the regular basketball fan, which they're there. But if you're sitting with somebody, if you're sitting with a wife, a girlfriend, or your kids, who don't know anything, like, I don't want to leave my daughter in the other room in her childhood. I want her watching basketball with me. I'm trying to entertain that kid or somebody like that. You've got a son and you like, 'Yo, make sure your son laugh and have fun watching basketball.' Because they don't understand all the intricacies of the X's and O's and things like that. It's like, 'Well, you know, they're blitzing this pick and roll.' 'Dad, what does that mean?' 'Oh, they they that mean they're going to double the pick and roll.' Or they're going under, they're going over, or they're hedging. We could sit there for five hours and talk like that, but nobody understands that. We want people to have fun watching basketball because, you know what? It's stupid basketball. We're not saving the world.

quotes.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Barkley discusses Draymond Green's personal attacks, emphasizing media's responsibility to be factual and fair
quotes.excerpt: I'm not sensitive. I say stuff about players all the time. I hope they don't take it personally.

text_blocks.speaker: JIMMY TRAINA
text_blocks.text: What what did you make of Shai's breaking the MVP on Sunday morning when it was supposed to be announced Sunday night? He got some flak for that, which I don't know, I think he's a reporter, he's supposed to do his job. What did you what did you make of that whole thing?

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: You know, I like him a lot, but I I didn't like that leaking. That network paid $2.5 billion for the for the next 11 years. $2.5, which is the reason we lost the NBA, because we couldn't come up with $2.5 billion for for 11 years. I think they deserve them exclusive. I think the NBA should be embarrassed that that got out. You know, you you know, you can't charge these networks that much money and then don't give them some exclusive on some things. I mean, I I just think that's unfair. You know, speaking of the the TV deals, so you guys, you know, we're in this I I still don't know if fans fully understand the Inside the NBA deal where you air on ESPN, but the show is still being produced by Turner and it's out of Atlanta with with with Turner and TNT, Warner Brothers Discovery, whatever you want to call it. I'm always going to say Turner, because I just I'm used to it.

text_blocks.speaker: JIMMY TRAINA
text_blocks.text: It could be Paramount. You never know, Jimmy. Right. Right. Right. It's Paramount. Yes. I forgot about that. True. Um, there's been there's been two themes. One, sort of like the disjointed schedule and whether the show's still the same, etcetera, etcetera. How would Charles Barkley assess the first year of this arrangement with Inside the NBA airing on ESPN?

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: It's been perfect. And I don't throw that word around lightly. They have been amazing to work with. I don't I I thought I wish we could work, you know, we only work one time in December, one time in January. You know, I think that Adam Silver's got to get a hold of this thing. I think the games are too disjointed right now. Like NBC, Peacock, Amazon, we've got, I think we we have disrespected the fans. They don't know when the games are on. I just think that's really unfair to the fans. And I understand, Adam, I love Adam. Adam's a great guy. But he he took the most money, but man, it it's hard for, like, for me. Like, when we weren't having games, I had to go, I had to go to my app and see where the game was at. Is it on NBC? Is it on Peacock? Is it on Amazon? The nights we haven't been working. So it's been frustrating for me. I can't imagine how frustrating it is for the regular fan. And I think we I'm not sure what the solution is because we they've taken all the money now, but they've got to do something because I think we've done a disservice to the fans. Yeah, early in the playoffs, it's a mess. I mean, now we're in a good spot because you guys, ESPN/ABC has the East. We know NBC has the West, so you don't have to think about it. Now, so let me ask you a question. So I don't even know this. I'm just asking. Do do NBC have exclusive or they have to share with Amazon? They they are, if I'm not mistaken, they they will be rotating every next year, Prime Video will have a Conference Final, NBC will not. Okay, okay. See, it's hard to keep up with it, man. I didn't even know that. I asked that question. At least that's a little bit better. Now, are they going to show all the games on NBC? I believe, yeah, they they won't do a Peacock exclusive for the Western Conference Final. And they should not. It should be on NBC. Correct. Absolutely. Um, yeah, the you know, I fight this battle constantly, but you either get told you're old or everyone has Amazon, so what difference does it make? But that's not sort of the point. But I don't want to rope you into that discussion. But let me ask you this. So the schedule's been one thing with Inside the NBA, and I think even ESPN, I think Burke Magnus has even said they want to have more of a flow next year for you guys and not not have happened what happened this year and and maybe switch it up and make it more frequent next year. There's also been, I've seen a couple of things out there saying like the show's not the same, meaning the content of the show. How would you respond to that?

text_blocks.speaker: JIMMY TRAINA
text_blocks.text: I had to get a kick out of Draymond. So when he made the he said the line about he didn't want to be you with the Rockets, which everyone sort of, you know, said, 'Well, look at Charles with the Rockets,' his numbers were as good as Draymond's with the Warriors. What I found interesting was afterwards, I guess after all the blowback, Draymond on his podcast said, 'Kenny didn't hear the line, that's why he didn't respond,' which I thought was really weak of Draymond to say that. I don't know, you know, how you feel about it, but Kenny heard the line. Let's not play that. Because you guys didn't sell, you know, if he wants to say it was a joke, you you know, in wrestling terms, WWE, you have to sell for your opponent. There was no selling there, so I guess, I don't know if he took that as like, you guys weren't good teammates there, but what's been the fallout from that whole situation?

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: Well, I was surprised how many people came to my defense, to be honest with you. You know, I'm not sensitive. You know, I say stuff about players all the time. I hope they don't take it personally. I know they have at certain times because I've gotten a call from them or their agent, or they've taken a shot at me on Twitter or something like that. But I don't overreact when guys get mad. So I didn't get mad when he took a shot at me. And I've said this before too, Jimmy. I was embarrassed my last two years in Houston because I was shot. I did not play well at all. People would point out those two years I felt like I was shot, they were better than Dray's career numbers. I'm like, but no, man, I didn't take it personally. Like I say, I don't get sensitive. You know, I can't get on TV, radio, your podcast and say things about people and and and like if they get mad or say something bad about me, act like a little little witchy. So I didn't take it personally. I take, and I, but I will admit this, I was really appreciate all the people who went after Draymond for for for for saying that. I I really appreciated that. Because I tell people this, and we can you can bring up anything I've ever said in the past. I've never taken personal shots at guys. That's my number one rule. Like, you can say a guy sucked at basketball, you can say a guy didn't play well and blah, blah, blah. But when you're in the media, it's such a powerful thing. It's a powerful thing because people are idiots. When I mean by that is, Jimmy, they believe they believe if they see it on television, somebody said it, it must be true. And I said, that's not true. Some of the guys, some of the stuff these guys, they're just playing, especially the politicians. They're just playing characters on television for whatever party, and both parties are awful, let's get that out of the way. But they're just playing a character for a party on television. So I take my job really serious. When I criticize a guy, that doesn't mean I'm right. I want to be factual and I want to be fair.

quotes.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Barkley hopes LeBron James returns to Cleveland to finish his career, believing it would make the Cavaliers Eastern Conference favorites
quotes.excerpt: I hope he goes back to Cleveland. I think that'd be a great way for him to finish his career.

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: That's a great question. Number one, I hope he goes back to Cleveland. I think that'd be a great way for him to finish his career. If he stays in LA, they're not going to be competitive. Because also, at some point, they've got to turn the team over to Luka and see let him let it be his team. And you're not going to get better as you get older. You're not going to get better. Your your numbers are going to continue to decline every year. But the main thing, the Lakers got to start the Luka Doncic era at some point. I think Cleveland would be a perfect fit for him. Because that team is too inconsistent, and he's such a great worker, he'll stop some of the inconsistencies. And if he were to go to Cleveland, Jimmy, honestly, I think they'd be the favorite in the East next year. Now, obviously, New York, Boston are going to have something to say about that, probably Detroit also. But if you were to put LeBron on that Cavs team right now, they'd probably be the favorite in the East. So I hope he goes back to Cleveland, to be honest with you. I think that'd just be a perfect way for him to end his career.

text_blocks.speaker: JIMMY TRAINA
text_blocks.text: Yeah, I I think that makes a lot of sense. I just he um I almost I almost thought it didn't really happen until the playoffs, but I thought during the regular season, he wasn't even getting I don't think he was getting credit for the way he was playing at his age. It was insane what he did this year at that age.

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: Yeah, he uh listen, he takes amazing care of his body. I've heard he spent a million dollars on his body. I think also, I think the the, you know, the NBA today is different than when I played. Like, we were getting off-road, we used to describe, we were getting like off-road mileage on our body. LeBron has highway miles on his body, just smooth sailing. There's no physicality in the game. And and that's not a knock, that's just a fact. There's no physicality in the game. So he don't have, he's never had any major injuries and things like that. So, but like I say, if you keep talking to Father Time, at some point he's going to talk back to you.

quotes.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Barkley credits David Stern, Magic Johnson, Larry Bird, and Michael Jordan for the NBA's current success
quotes.excerpt: The three most important figures in NBA history are Michael, Magic, and Larry Bird.
quotes.quote: The three most important figures in NBA history are Michael, Magic, and Larry Bird. There's a lot of great, great players, but those are the three most prominent players in NBA history because Magic and Michael, excuse me, Magic and Larry saved the NBA. Because, you know, people, you know, it's interesting, everybody look at how great the NBA is today. They don't realize when the NBA came along before David Stern, the average salary was only $250,000. That's the average of all players. And we it was only on on Sunday on CBS. And how about this? Can you imagine the Finals being tape delayed? That's how, I mean, and fans think like there's always been games on five days a week like it is now. But that's all because of David Stern, Magic Johnson, Larry Bird, and obviously we call them once in a lifetime guy, Michael.

quotes.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Barkley shares his positive experience with the weight loss drug Zepbound, losing over 80 pounds
quotes.excerpt: The weight loss thing has freed me up while I feel great walking around now.

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: I don't do I don't I don't do the pill. I take a shot once a week. I started at 355, Jimmy, and I'm 270 now. It's been a long journey. Because like I say, I gained like 100 pounds when I got my hips because I played at 250, but I wanted to get to 270 and this drug Zepbound has changed my life. I feel better than I have in 20 years. You know, and I tell people this who are fat, you don't realize how bad you feel until you start feeling better. Yeah, I got used to just feeling awful. I did. I was like, you like, what? Everything's going to hurt all the time. Everything, I just get used to that. And then when you lose like the first 20, 30 pounds, you're like, wow. And I couldn't lose, I couldn't eat enough bird food and work out enough to lose to get from 355 to 270. And they got these drugs out here at your disposal because, man, you want to be healthy when you get older. I mean, I just turned 63. I'm not getting any younger. And like I say, I I want to eat, and I definitely don't want to work out all the time. So I I shout out to Ro.co and my girl Molly who takes care of me.

text_blocks.speaker: JIMMY TRAINA
text_blocks.text: So with the with the shot, it's you your appetite is much less, correct?

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: You know, that is a great question. I have no idea. You know, Jimmy, I've been seriously, I've been asked that question 5,975 times. And I in the beginning, I said, you know, I should come up with a good lie. And then I said, you know what, just tell the truth because you want if if people are going to, I will tell you this, this is the only endorsement I ever had that cost me money, Jimmy. I'm not going to lie. This is the only endorsement I've ever, I've got 20 of my friends on this program that I'm paying for. This is the only endorsement I've ever done that I'm losing money. I'm losing money.

text_blocks.speaker: JIMMY TRAINA
text_blocks.text: You're making 21. I could use it. The reason I asked about if it if it changes your appetite, I was going to ask if there's something you miss eating. If there's something you miss.

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: No, no, I mean, I have to eat. I I have to eat. Am I eating better? 100%. Am I working out? 100%. But I have zero idea. You'd have I'd have to talk to a doctor, honestly. I have zero idea what this drug does for me. I just know it works. Like I said, I went from 355, I'm at 270 now, but I have zero idea. I take that shot. Like I said, I you you got to eat. I mean, I'm a big old dude. I need to eat. But I I I wish somebody would explain to me exactly what it does to your body.

quotes.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Barkley challenges the "shoving things down your throat" argument against LGBTQ+ visibility, highlighting the irony of gay people having to hide
quotes.excerpt: You think it's being shoved down your throat, yet as you made the point, there are gay people in every sport and they all have to stay in the closet.

text_blocks.speaker: JIMMY TRAINA
text_blocks.text: You think it's being shoved down your throat, yet as you made the point, there are gay people in every sport and they all have to stay in the closet. So how's it being how's it being shoved down your throat? It makes you like you how do you argue with people like that when it's, you know?

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: You don't argue with people, you you like, hey, we agree to disagree. And and and listen, it's kind of like we've had this argument in pro sports about gays in the locker room. I said, 'Well, first of all, it's disrespectful to think a gay guy in the locker room is going to be oogling all the guys.' I said, 'He ain't thinking about us!' I said, 'What do you think this guy just like, I heard football players like, I guess there's 53 players on the NFL team and a couple guys came out and said they don't they wouldn't want to play with a gay guy. He'd be looking around looking at his teammates.' I said, 'That's disrespectful to gay people like they're just out here looking for other men or other women.' So it just bothers me. And like I say, man, if I feel like there's discrimination, I'm going to stand up because and the reason I do that, to be honest with you, I'm hoping somebody stands up for me. Like, with all this redistricting going on and Jerry Mandering going on around the country, I'm hoping it shouldn't just be black people standing up saying, 'Hey, man, that ain't right, that ain't fair.' You know, that's the thing that I would like to get to a point, I'm like, no, I want, like, obviously my son-in-law is Jewish, if I see anybody out here being anti-Semitic, I'm going to say something. You know, I'm going to say something. I I'm not going to sit back and let let it happen on my watch.

quotes.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Barkley predicts the Oklahoma City Thunder and Cleveland Cavaliers will meet in the NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: I'm not going to live in the moment. I'm going to stick with OKC and the Cavs.

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: I'm not going to live in the moment. I'm going to stick with OKC and the Cavs. That's, I had the Cavs the whole time. I listen, I told you, you talk about, they drive Dr. Phil crazy with all them damn personalities on that team. Because I never know, like, I'm I was like, I know the Cavs are going to wrap up in Game 6. This is over once they won Game 5. Then they come out and play like absolute trash in Game 6. And I'm like, Detroit is going to the Finals. Then the Cavs come out and play like the best team in the world in Game 7. And I'm like, 'Yo, man, I can't figure this team out.' But I did pick them before the playoffs start to come out of the East. But I will say this, I never root for teams. I think it'd be great for the NBA if the Knicks make it to the Finals. But I'm going to go OKC and Cleveland.

text_blocks.speaker: JIMMY TRAINA
text_blocks.text: All right. We'll see how it plays out. I'm sure the New Yorkers will love that. Charles, appreciate it as always. And again, what people need to understand is first time ever, Inside the NBA will be on every night during the NBA. Eastern Conference Finals always, but now the NBA Finals. So we're looking forward to that, Chuck. Thanks a lot for doing this. I appreciate it. I know you're busy.

text_blocks.speaker: CHARLES BARKLEY
text_blocks.text: Anytime, brother. Hey, you keep up the great work and thanks for having me.
